headings.title: Continue a request that needs input

html:
Integration execution API

Use this API when another program needs to submit an Agent request and read a JSON result. It delegates to the same Controller request and continuation services used by the product. Normal access, accepted terms, tool selection and execution policy still apply. The API does not create a separate executor or permission bypass.

The running service's /docs and /openapi.json describe the exact schemas. This guide explains the request lifecycle and the fields clients must interpret.

Submit a request

Send POST /api/agent/integrations/execute with a JSON body such as:

{
  "prompt": "Describe the task status.",
  "agent_mode": "agent",
  "timeout_seconds": 0
}
Field Meaning
prompt Required text, 1–24,000 characters.
agent_mode Defaults to agent. The API also retains conversation and advisory compatibility values; the UI's Plan selection is not an agent_mode enum value.
conversation_id Optional existing conversation identity, up to 160 characters. Normal conversation admission still applies.
context Optional context object passed through the ordinary request boundary. It is not a grant of execution authority.
behavior_effort Optional low, medium, high, extra_high or ultra; the existing behavior policy resolves it.
timeout_seconds Response wait after submission, from 0 to 1,800 seconds; default 120. It is not an execution deadline or an end-to-end HTTP timeout.

The Controller owns model routing. Configure models through Model Configuration; per-request model, endpoint, credential and reserved generation overrides are rejected at the public boundary. Capability selection and execution permissions remain with their existing owners.

Interpret the response

Save request_id from every submission or continuation. The response includes a trace_url, a possibly empty conversation_id, body status, final text/error fields and any available output, display, progress, metrics or action information.

HTTP response Meaning
200 from execute/confirm/clarify The wait reached a completed, failed, cancelled or awaiting-input state. Inspect the body; 200 does not mean the task succeeded.
202 from execute/confirm/clarify The wait expired. The current snapshot is returned and execution remains owned by the Controller.
200 from result lookup A current snapshot was found. It may still be running.
404 The requested trace is not available in retained history, including if it disappears during a wait.
422 The submitted body failed schema/public-input validation.

The body status is one of running, completed, failed, cancelled, awaiting_confirmation or awaiting_clarification. Internal nonterminal states are represented as running; this envelope is not a detailed scheduler-state API. A pending confirmation or clarification flag can keep an otherwise completed trace in an awaiting-input state. When present, needs_action carries the corresponding actions or question details.

Read current state with GET /api/agent/integrations/results/{request_id}. This GET returns immediately; it neither restarts work nor follows a newer continuation for you. A wait timeout also does not cancel the task. Clients should accommodate normal submission time in addition to their chosen response-wait interval.

Unavailable request handlers return 503; a submission/continuation that fails to return a request identity produces 500. Ordinary admission or continuation errors can also propagate from the existing request service.

Continue a request that needs input

For a confirmation, send POST /api/agent/integrations/confirm/{request_id} with an explicit decision:

{"action": "approve", "timeout_seconds": 120}

Use "action": "deny" to reject it. The schema defaults omitted action to approve, so clients should always send the intended action. Denial returns a cancelled envelope for the original request immediately. Approval uses the existing confirmation service and waits on the request identity it returns.

For a clarification, send POST /api/agent/integrations/clarify/{request_id}:

{"answer": "Read only", "timeout_seconds": 120}

The answer is required. Optional selected_option_id, parameter_choice_id, parameter_key, parameter_field and persist_for_event fields support the existing question/parameter-choice workflow. Use the choices offered by that workflow; the continuation owner validates them. Both continuation payloads also accept a context object.

Use the returned request ID for subsequent reads. Approval and clarification can create a child request, and the original result URL does not automatically track it. Retain the original ID as well when correlating the full interaction.

Outputs, retention and retries

final_response and error are response text; optional error_detail carries structured diagnostics. outputs projects raw payloads still present on the trace, with data_ref, source operation identity, type, command diagnostics, preview, metadata and a full_payload_available flag when supplied by the producer.

The adapter uses a diagnostics object in preference to a preview object for command fields. It normalizes and limits stdout, stderr and error previews to a 12,000-character prefix plus a truncation marker. Structured output, preview and metadata are not subjected to that text limit. They retain the source representation; the integration adapter adds no independent credential-redaction pass.

An empty outputs list is not proof that no tool ran. Raw provider payloads are not part of the durable trace journal, and available previews can differ after recovery or retention. Use the reported status, evidence references and existing artifact interfaces for the result you need; this response is not a complete durable transcript.

The execute payload has no idempotency-key field. If a reply is lost, use the known request ID to inspect the original work before submitting again. A missing reply or missing retained trace does not prove an external change did not happen.

Older database requests

The historical POST /api/agent/sql/query route remains available. It invokes a registered Database tool directly through the execution engine and returns that tool's execution result, rather than the integration response envelope above.

Its required parameter_key identifies the saved database profile. operation defaults to execute and accepts only:

  • execute: call database.execute, forwarding sql and refresh_schema.
  • discover_schema: call database.discover_schema, forwarding refresh_schema.

Other operation values receive HTTP 422. Optional instruction supplies prompt context, and the compatibility approval_mode defaults to manual; execution-engine checks remain authoritative. This route has no integration response-wait field. See Parameter Store and databases for profile setup.

Implementation owners are IntegrationRoutes, request/response models and the retained SQL route. The request lifecycle explains ordinary admission and continuation ownership.
